invariant: Plain substitution recognizes registered function names; unknown expression calls fail. Getenv is a registered one-argument string function: denied or absent environment entries yield empty; permitted entries retain their exact text.
causal_divergence: The original adapter silently returned empty for every unimplemented call. Making that fatal exposed an existing valid bundled-theme getenv call, and treating every percent token as registered incorrectly applies expression errors to ordinary text.
planned_change: Represent pinned Java builtin name registration (and existing Rust extensions) for plain substitution. Add Getenv argument validation and source-derived name/profile filtering, process environment lookup, and native path/line separator properties. Rust has no arbitrary JVM system-property namespace; that unsupported environment surface remains explicit residue. Keep unknown expression calls fatal.
perturbation_axes: Registered versus unknown names in plain text and expression contexts
Permitted/denied/absent names, separator properties, and profile selection
oracle_plan: Reuse preserved outline-state fixture and all prior checker records without changes.
Stage fresh source controls for remote-only reference runs when SSH recovers; never invent unavailable references.
Record environment scope and missing JVM property configuration explicitly.
constraints: No unowned production, frozen evidence, guard, comparator or baseline changes.
This is maker work, not acceptance or independent review.
